name: Make drones interesting by role: a bass pedal point under changing harmony (or a repeated arpeggiated root), a non-key-tracked mid-range drone as a through-line with the bass and an upper note moving around it, layered drones tuned to a static chord with a progression underneath for polychords, and wavetable-position sweeps for texture
goal: Decide what a drone does in the track and write around it: as a pedal point (one bass note held or repeated for the whole track while chords and textures change above), as a mid-range 'connective tissue' oscillator (pitch tracking off) that the bass line and a note above it rub against, or as a stack of drones forming a fixed chord over a moving progression to create polychords and unresolved tension. Keep exposed drones alive with slow wavetable-position sweeps. Delta vs the existing 'held root under a changing chord' harmony variant: the mid-range fixed-pitch through-line and drone-stack polychords.

source.title: How to SYNTH DRONE without boring everyone

prerequisites: Synth where one oscillator can have key tracking off (fixed pitch), or a separate drone voice
Wavetable synth with a modulatable position

inputs.name: key
inputs.description: Track key and the drone note(s)

outputs.name: drone_arrangement
outputs.description: Drone layer plus the moving parts written around it

constraints: Original synthesis/processing recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any DAW/synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks, impulse responses or samples copied.
Steady pitch (Matt's taste): the source likes wobbly tape loops on drones; skip tape wow/flutter or keep it tiny and never on the foundation.
A drone used as the foundation locks the low end; then interest must come from harmony, texture and rhythm above it.
Do not stack several drones in the low end; keep stacked drones in the mids/high mids.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only the pad before that.

steps.action: Choose the drone's role: foundation (bass pedal point) or textural through-line in the mids/high mids.

Pedal point: hold or repeat one bass note for the whole piece (an arpeggiator repeating the root counts); change chords, textures and rhythm above it, e.g. hold the dominant to build tension before resolving to the tonic.
steps.expect: Tension from harmony moving over a fixed bass

steps.action: Through-line: switch off key tracking on one oscillator and tune it to a mid-range note; play bass notes and a note above that move around it, auditioning chords for the rubs they create. A second fixed partial (e.g. A440) can be added rhythmically.
steps.expect: A constant middle tone with harmony shifting around it; bass line free to move

steps.action: Polychords: tune several mid/high drones to a static chord and play a different chord progression underneath so the two combine into polychords that never fully resolve.
Texture: on exposed drones, find sweet spots in a rich wavetable and sweep the position slowly with an LFO.
steps.expect: Evolving timbre on a static pitch

steps.action: Change the bass note under the drone at key moments; a single new pedal note recolours everything above it.
steps.expect: Big harmonic shifts from one note

verification: The drone pitch never changes; harmonic interest comes from parts around it.
At least one moment where a new bass note recolours the drone.
Wavetable position moves slowly on exposed drones.
